content: In this course, you will learn the principles of network structure and protocol design, as well as the principles of Internet communication.
You will master the layers of the OSI model and be able to design and implement local area networks using switches, routers and servers.
You will learn how to design cabling and routing plans and how to handle network equipment configurations.
You will also understand how to efficiently connect local area networks to backbone networks.
The contents stated through the OSI model:
Layer 1: physical cabling (copper, fiber), wireless local area networks, basic modulations in data transfer, and devices.
Layer 2: Ethernet switching, network segmentation (VLANs), loop detection (Spanning Tree), and MAC addressing.
Layer 3: IPv4 and IPv6 addressing, subnetting, routing (Static, OSPF and BGP), DHCP, and ARP.
Layers 5 to 7: SSH, HTTP, DNS, and SMTP.
In addition, best practices in network design and configuration management are covered in the course.

objective: In the Graphics Programming Course, you learn the basics of real-time 3D graphics and programmable pipeline programming. The course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of computer graphics, including how to develop and implement 3D graphics applications that are both visually appealing and interactive.

Throughout the course, you learn about the key concepts of computer graphics, such as geometric transformations, shading models, and rasterization. You will also learn how to program graphics pipelines using modern, high-level graphics APIs such as OpenGL and Vulkan, and how to utilize modern graphics hardware to render 3D scenes in real-time.

You also gain an understanding of how to use graphics frameworks and libraries to accelerate the development of your 3D graphics applications.

content: The course focuses on modern front-end development, introducing foundational concepts, tools and programming practices needed to build interactive and maintainable user interfaces. Learning combines exercises, tool use and teamwork with current front-end technologies. AI is integrated as a supportive tool throughout the course.
Fundamental programming constructs, data types, expressions and control structures in a front end programming language.
Handling strings, objects and arrays or other common collections, and applying data manipulation techniques.
Function design, modularization, scope and closures, and structuring applications into reusable units.
Detecting, analyzing and handling runtime errors; debugging principles and tools.
Interacting with UI elements, manipulating the document structure and implementing event-based functionality.
Managing imports and exports and organizing modular application architecture.
Techniques for handling asynchronous operations and coordinating UI updates.

Using professional development tools such as linters, bundlers, testing tools, version control systems and AI assisted tools for code generation support, refactoring suggestions, debugging hints, accessibility checks and documentation drafts.
2. Component Based Front End Development (Lectures and Teamwork)
Principles of building applications using components, independent of any specific framework.
Using declarative or template-based syntax to describe UI hierarchies and layout patterns.
Managing state within components and across applications; applying best practices for predictable data flow.
Structuring applications into reusable, maintainable components and modules; separation of concerns.

Using framework specific and general-purpose tools for development and debugging. Leveraging AI enhanced utilities to generate component scaffolds, analyze code quality, identify issues and support design decisions.
Developing a component based front-end application in teams, applying version control workflows, code reviews, issue tracking and responsible AI use guidelines
